newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Waigel arrives at ECOFIN meeting in Brussels.
newsitem.headline: Waigel arrives at ECOFIN meeting in Brussels.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel arrived in Brussels for talks with other European economic and finance ministers at around 1545 GMT on Monday.

Waigel, who as proposer of a so-called stability pact was expected to play a key role in the talks, arrived late for the talks, which began at 0900 GMT, as he had been giving a speech in the Bonn parliament in honour of a late party colleague.

Asked on arrival whether he expected the ministers to agree on the stability pact -- intended to ensure fiscal discipline in Europe once Economic and Monetary Union has started in 1999 -- Waigel told reporters, "I hope so."

Although the EU has agreed on some basic elements of the pact -- such as the fact that member countries in EMU will face sanctions and possible fines if they spend beyond stated budget targets -- there are many details still to be ironed out.

Germany has taken a characteristically hardline position on several points, calling for higher fines than other EU members would like and insisting on a clear definition of economic recession which would allow countries to exceed the target.
Asked whether he believed there was room for compromise on these issues, Waigel said, "We have good arguments". He did not elaborate.
Germany has called for an exceptionally bad recession to be defined as a contraction of at least two percent in gross domestic product in the course of a year.
It has sought fines of 0.25 percent of GDP for each percentage point in deficits compared to GDP which a country notches in excess of a three percent target.
